candidate.content: For cool-then-place tasks targeting lettuce, navigating to open horizontal surfaces (countertops) before closed storage receptacles can locate and acquire the target. In this instance, inspecting countertop_1 (no lettuce) then countertop_2 (lettuce present) yielded successful acquisition in 3 total actions without opening any cabinets or drawers.
candidate.scope: ALFWorld pick_cool_then_place_in_recep tasks where the target is lettuce and the environment contains multiple countertops alongside closed receptacles. This trajectory demonstrates feasibility of an open-surface-first search for lettuce; it does not assert that this ordering is globally optimal or preferred over other strategies, nor does it cover the downstream cooling and placement steps.

direct_grounding.semantic_fact: Navigating to countertop_1 revealed bowl_3, bowl_2, creditcard_2, creditcard_1, dishsponge_1, and glassbottle_1, with no lettuce present.
Navigating to countertop_2 revealed bread_1, cellphone_1, cup_2, cup_1, dishsponge_2, knife_2, knife_1, lettuce_2, lettuce_1, and plate_2, confirming lettuce was present on this open surface.
The action take lettuce_1 from countertop_2 succeeded, acquiring the target into inventory.

minimal_global_context: The initial observation listed the task as 'put a cool lettuce in countertop' and enumerated available locations including six cabinets, three countertops, three drawers, one fridge, shelves, stoveburners, and other fixtures.
The admissible actions at the start included navigation to all listed receptacles but no open actions were required or performed during the observed trajectory.
